newsitem.title: JAPAN: G7 agreed that strong yen correction over - MOF.
newsitem.headline: G7 agreed that strong yen correction over - MOF.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Monday that the Group of Seven (G7) nations had agreed at their meeting that the correction process of the strong yen was now over.

Asked whether Japan was seeking stability in foreign exchange rates rather than a stronger yen, Mitsuzuka reiterated the G7 nations' weekend agreement, which called for currency stability, and added: "As included in our agreement, the correction process of the strong yen has finished."
He declined to comment on short-term movements in the foreign exchange markets, but said that the Japanese authorities expect the G7 agreement to have a "good effect" on financial markets.
Mitsuzuka added that stability in foreign exchange rates was important for economies in general.

Asked whether Japan had promised the United States any measures to boost domestic demand in Japan, Mitsuzuka said : "Not at all." He added that he was not asked by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin in their meeting on Saturday to take any such measures.
However, he said Japan was seeking to achieve an economic recovery led by private demand.
